text:
aj: Heads-up — saw a spike in pending GPU pods this morning in eu-west-1, looks like new nodes spun up but pods stuck pending with AttachVolume / IP errors.
maria: omg, saw the same on the perf tests. some pods got scheduled to new node but kubelet failed to allocate eni: "ENI IPs exhausted".
vikram: are they using the old node pools or the Karpenter provisioner? which pool got used?
aj: Karpenter provisioner. We migrated a couple of workloads last week. Provisioner config has consolidation enabled and spot fallback.
carla: likely ENI/trunking + instance family choice. If Karpenter picks m5n types we don't get trunking, limited ip/eni count -> quick exhaustion with many small pods.
maria: we intentionally let it pick small instances to save $/GPU. But today we had lots of small sidecars + each pod calls external services, so more network connections than expected.
vikram: two axes: (1) reduce per-node pod density (2) bias Karpenter away from instance types with low ENI capacity. We can do both via provider constraints.
aj: suggested quick fix: add nodeSelector label to provisioner to prefer p4d/p3dn families in eu-west-1 for GPU-heavy workloads. That increases ENI headroom but costs more.
carla: or allow a warm pool / warm nodes with fewer pods per node. Karpenter has launchTemplate overrides — we can add a smaller maxPods or set a taint to schedule non-critical pods elsewhere.
maria: taints seems safer: pump a taint gpu-heavy=true:NoSchedule on Karpenter nodes and add tolerations to gpu workloads only. That prevents random sidecars from landing there.
aj: +1. Also adding a topologySpreadConstraint on critical workloads to avoid packing multiple high-connection pods on same node.
vikram: FYI ip-assignments: small instances have AWS ENI limits like 2-15 IPs depending on family. For g4dn.12xlarge might be fine, but g4dn.xlarge is terrible. Karpenter choosing xlarge to match GPU count is dangerous.
sre-jen: we should also gate the provisioner with a max per-az limit so we don't blow past VPC elastic IP quotas during burst.
carla: actionable plan:
- short term: add a provider constraint to prefer instance families with trunking + higher IP capacity for GPU provisioner
- short term: add taint "gpu-only" on provisioned nodes, add toleration to gpu daemonsets
- medium term: configure warm pool (reserved nodes) for GPU workload to avoid cold start + consolidation churn
- medium term: add a policy in Karpenter to limit consolidation frequency for GPU provisioner to avoid oscillation
aj: I'll prototype a Provisioner snippet for the quick fix:

```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-provisioner-eu-west
spec:
  requirements:
  - key: node.kubernetes.io/instance-type
    operator: In
    values: [p4d.24xlarge, p3dn.24xlarge, g5.12xlarge]
  taints:
  - key: "gpu-only"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  consolidation:
    enabled: true
  provider:
    subnetSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: eu-west-1
    securityGroupSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: default
  limits:
    resources:
      cpu: "2000"
```

maria: nice, that'll bias away from tiny instances. We should also add an admission check to prevent pods without tolerations landing on GPU nodes.
vikram: can we enforce that via mutating webhook to inject toleration for only known gpu workloads? riskier.
carla: easier: update the scheduler config / PodAffinity rules or label non-gpu pods with "no-gpu" and add nodeAffinity to non-gpu workloads.
aj: cost note: moving to larger instances ups $/hour but reduces pod churn and ENI/IP errors; fewer nodes means less ENI pressure and lower overall API overhead. We'll model 24h run vs burst.
sre-jen: create a short runbook for oncall: if ENI exhaustion observed -> 1) disable consolidation on provisioner 2) scale up a control pool with high-eni instance type 3) re-add taints after stabilized.
maria: +1. I'll draft a small runbook and a canary patch for the provisioner. @deploy-bot can you create a canary deploy to staging with the yaml above?
deploy-bot: canary job started — will create 2 nodes in staging and run 50 pod stress test, notify in 10m. :robot_face:
aj: thanks. After canary we should also run the perf harness with pod-density sim to validate ip headroom.
carla: and let's add metrics: track node allocatableIPs, podsPerNode, eniCount, and kubelet attach failures. Alert if attach failures > 5 in 5m.
vikram: last comment: consider using IPv6 internal or CNI plugin improvements long term, but that's a bigger change.
maria: ok wrapping up — I'll push PR with taints + instance-type constraint and the runbook. Tagging infra-eng for review. :thumbsup:
aj: cheers — will monitor once canary lands."
